Import iSNV data from VCF files

Source: R/import-vcf.R
readWithinHost.Rd

Reads one or more VCF files produced by variant callers (iVar through a VCF converter, LoFreq, Freebayes, or others) with VariantAnnotation::readVcf() and constructs a WithinHostExperiment. A VCF already read into R is converted with as(vcf, "WithinHostExperiment"), and a VRanges with as(vr, "WithinHostExperiment"); see coerce-WHE.

Usage

readWithinHost(vcfFiles, colData, caller = "auto", genome = NULL)

Arguments

vcfFiles

Character vector. Paths to VCF files (one per sample).

colData

DataFrame or data.frame. Sample metadata. Must contain sample_id. May also contain host_id, role, pair_id, replicate_group, replicate_id, etc.

caller

Character scalar. Which field layout the VCF uses: "ivar", "lofreq", "freebayes", "auto" (default) or "generic". See Details.

genome

Optional DNAStringSet holding the reference sequence, as returned by Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(). The length of each sequence is recorded in seqlengths(rowRanges()), whether or not a call lies on it. It must name the sequences the calls lie on and be long enough to hold them; see Details.

Value

A WithinHostExperiment.

Details

Each VCF file corresponds to one sample. The colData argument provides sample metadata and must contain a sample_id column whose length matches the number of files. A file holding more than one sample is an error; read it with readVcf() and convert the object instead.

caller = "ivar" refers to a VCF carrying iVar's per-sample fields (REF_DP, ALT_DP, ALT_FREQ, ALT_QUAL). ivar variants itself writes a TSV, not a VCF, so such files come from a converter, for instance ivar_variants_to_vcf.py in the nf-core/viralrecon pipeline. An iVar TSV is read directly by readWithinHostTable(format = "ivar").

Caller. With caller = "auto" the layout is chosen from the VCF header: a header naming iVar, LoFreq or Freebayes (as the ##source line of each does) selects that layout, and any other gives "generic". The layouts read: iVar, FORMAT ALT_FREQ, ALT_DP and REF_DP, with depth their sum (INFO DP where they are missing); LoFreq, INFO AF and DP, with counts derived from them; Freebayes, FORMAT AO, RO and DP (INFO DP where FORMAT has none), with frequency AO / DP; generic, the first of those field names that the file carries.

Several alternative alleles. A record with several alternative alleles is split into one site per allele with VariantAnnotation::expand(). A per-allele value is split correctly only when the header declares it Number=A, as the VCF specification requires; readVcf() keeps just the first value of a field declared otherwise. When such a record carries one of the per-allele fields read here (INFO AF; FORMAT AO, AF, ALT_DP, ALT_FREQ, ALT_QUAL) under another Number, the function stops rather than give the second allele the first allele's value. Correct the header, or split the records first (for example with bcftools norm -m-). On a biallelic record a field declared Number=1 or Number=. is read as it is. A field declared Number=R stops the import whatever the records, since it gives the reference allele's value first and that value would be read as the alternative allele's; declare it Number=A, with one value per alternative allele.

Sequence lengths. Lengths are recorded in seqlengths(rowRanges()) from the VCF header's ##contig lines and from genome; two sources that disagree are an error. Every sequence a header line or genome names is recorded, including those without a call, since the genome length sums over all of them. Functions that need the genome length read it from there, so genome is checked before anything is recorded: it is an error when it names none of the sequences the calls lie on, or when a call lies past the end of its sequence, since either way it is not the reference the calls were made against. A sequence the calls lie on that genome does not name is left without a length, with a warning.

What is not read. The FILTER column is not read, so a record the caller rejected (LoFreq's sb_fdr or min_snvqual, for instance) is imported as a call, and flagISNV judges it by its depth, frequency and read-count thresholds alone. To drop such records, read the file with readVcf(), keep those whose FILTER is PASS or ., write them to a file and import that:


vcf <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(path)
keep <- VariantAnnotation::filt(vcf) %in% c("PASS", ".")
passed <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
VariantAnnotation::writeVcf(vcf[keep, ], passed)
whe <- readWithinHost(passed, colData, caller = "lofreq")

This keeps every argument of readWithinHost(). Converting the subset directly, with as(vcf[keep, ], "WithinHostExperiment"), also works, but the caller is then taken from the ##source header line (the generic layout when it names none), the sample names from the VCF, and no genome can be given.

Per-strand counts, such as LoFreq's DP4 or Freebayes's SAF and SAR, are not imported. The strand-bias step of flagISNV() runs only when the assays fwdAltCount and revAltCount are present, so on an imported object it is skipped and leaves no qcLog row, although qcFilters() records the filter's maxStrandBias; flagStrandBiasSCI stops for want of those assays and of fwdTotalCount and revTotalCount. Assays added with assay(x, "fwdAltCount") <- and so on before flagISNV() are used.

Insertions and deletions are imported as rows of width 1 at their POS, with ref and alt as the VCF writes them (CTA and C for a deletion of two bases), and nothing tells them apart from substitutions: they pass flagISNV() like any other call and enter the diversity statistics. An iVar TSV read by readWithinHostTable() writes the same deletion in its own notation, so the two routes do not match it by allele. To keep substitutions only, subset to rows whose ref and alt are one base each:


rr <- SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(whe)
whe <- whe[nchar(rr$ref) == 1L & nchar(rr$alt) == 1L, ]

When technical replicates are not available, Roder et al. (2023, mBio 14:e01046-23) recommend using a combination of multiple variant callers with stringent cutoffs to reduce false positives. To implement multi-caller consensus, import VCFs from each caller separately and intersect the resulting objects using standard GRanges overlap operations.

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar")
whe
#> WithinHostExperiment with 15 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(5): altFreq, totalDepth, refCount, altCount, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 0 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0 

## The same file read into R first, then converted
v <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(vcf)
as(v, "WithinHostExperiment")
#> WithinHostExperiment with 15 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(5): altFreq, totalDepth, refCount, altCount, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 0 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0 

## Only the records the caller passed (FILTER is PASS or ".")
keep <- VariantAnnotation::filt(v) %in% c("PASS", ".")
as(v[keep, ], "WithinHostExperiment")
#> WithinHostExperiment with 15 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(5): altFreq, totalDepth, refCount, altCount, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 0 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0
